note: Faint CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2024-10-01T01:09Z. Also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 for a few frames. The source of this CME is likely an M7.6 flare from AR 3842 (S18E30) that peaked at 2024-09-30T23:59Z. The flare and associated EUV wave are best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-09-30T23:47Z and are followed by some dimming across the SE quadrant of the Earth-facing disk and some post eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement made with SWPC_CAT using very limited SOHO imagery due to the faintness of the CME and only one frame of STEREO A COR2 due to its ongoing campaign. Measurements yield a ~10 degree range in longitudes from ~E20 to ~E30 and corresponding range of speeds all less than 375 km/s.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-01T01:25Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some ejecta  from AR 3834 (~S15W65) best seen in SDO AIA 193 that starts at 2024-10-01T00:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. STEREO A COR2 imagery is limited due to it ongoing campaign.

note: Narrow, fairly slow CME seen only in SOHO LASCO imagery to the northwest along the northwest streamer, not seen in STEREO A due to a data gap as well as poor image quality/graininess. Likely associated with moving field lines seen in SDO AIA 171 beyond the northwest limb around 2024-10-01T15:00Z that indicate this CME is far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO plane of sky measurement out to 5 solar radii as early STEREO A imagery was poor and was followed by a data gap during the CME propagation.

note: CME seen to the south-southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and not seen in STEREO A due to low quality imagery; the source appears to be associated with Active Region 3835 (S21W55) despite an ongoing flare and possibly minor eruption from the eastern portion of the disk near the same time; there is opening field lines off the southwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171 that this CME could potentially be associated with.

cmeAnalyses.note: One-spacecraft measurement which considers that this eruption is associated with AR3835 on the Earth-facing disk, though this eruption may possibly be far-sided.

note: Developing CME with bulk seen predominantly to the southeast in early frames with a very faint, oval-shaped/asymmetric halo shock portion, associated with an X7.1-class flare and associated eruption from AR3842 (S17E18). Coronal signatures include an EUV wave and large-scale dimming in SDO AIA 171/193 with magnetic field line movement off the southern and southeast limbs and dimming of footpoints bridging the Active Region 3842 (S17E18) in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement with a lower half-width to try and more closely match the observed type II shock speed for this event of ~1200 km/s. A very approximate analysis based on the fit of the complex-shaped faint shock with two coronagraphs.

Updated bulk measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery so only early imagery in SOHO LASCO C2 was used in this measurement. Multiple measurements produced speeds ranging from 487 to 632 km/s.
Preliminary shock measurement using SOHO C2 early frames capturing the faint and very wide shock; was not able to fit the full shock with half-widths less than 60 degrees given the oval shape.
Preliminary bulk measurement of the CME using only early SOHO C2 frames in a small window from 2024-10-01T23:00Z to 23:36Z and STEREO A COR2 imagery out to 2024-10-02T01:09Z.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A imagery. The source is likely an eruption and rising loops visible starting around 2024-10-02T04:30Z from Active Region 13842 (S15E16) as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. Additionally, there is an M3.6 flare from Active Region 13842 starting around 2024-10-02T05:30Z which is also likely related to this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the S/SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in a few frames of STEREO A imagery. The source is an eruption and subsequent M3.2 flare from AR 3842 (S18E09) starting around 2024-10-02T13:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery from 2024-10-02T14:08Z to 2024-10-02T17:08Z, in addition to being in campaign mode for the Parker Solar Probe perihelion pass which affects COR2A image quality and cadence.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement made using source longitude as seen in UV imagery, as well as best fit using multiple SOHO LASCO C2/C3 frames and only one good frame of STEREO A COR2. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery from 2024-10-02T14:08Z to 2024-10-02T17:08Z, in addition to being in campaign mode for the Parker Solar Probe perihelion pass which affects COR2A image quality and cadence.

note: CME visible to the N/NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Source is opening field lines seen at a high northern latitude and beyond the N/NW limb in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2024-10-02T16:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 which is in campaign mode, but the CME was visible for several frames.

note: CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-03T08:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. N25E70 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2024-10-03T07:30Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284. This filament erupted gradually, so there is a small amount of material seen preceding the main bulk of the CME from which the measurement was based.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Due to the ongoing campaign, there were no useable STEREO A COR2 frames for this measurement.

note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2020-10-03T09:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption beginning at approx. 2024-10-03T09:19Z centered at approx. S30W15 with Southern deflection as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: Full halo CME observed in SOHO LASCO, and full halo directed slightly more eastward in STEREO COR2A. The source is an X9.0 flare from AR 3842 observed in many wavelengths but mainly SDO AIA 131, starting at 2024-10-03T12:08Z and peaking at T12:18Z. Also observed as an EUV wave and dimming in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284, with surface brightening in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

SHOCK measurment triangulated between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The shock front is notably wide with a "layered" appearance in both SOHO and STEREO with some apparent concentric fronts, along with being a bit "wider" than it was "taller" with an overall oval-shape in SOHO. The best fit between both shock fronts is presented here, though it does not capture 100% of the shock front which may be even wider.

note: CME seen to the NW within the outflow of the halo CME: 2024-10-03T12:48Z associated with a filament eruption lifting off near N25W52 or so seen best in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI 304. The CME is not seen in STEREO A well, due to poor image quality and a data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using only SOHO C2/C3; the CME is not seen in early STEREO A frames, and then STEREO A data drops out, so this one-spacecraft measurement is approximate in that it has a fixed longitude; it is possible there is more westward deflection (higher longitude) and the latitude is lower.

note: Large loop CME seen to the NE in SOHO/STEREO A embedded in outflow of halo CME: 2024-10-03T12:48Z. Associated with a filament eruption/snapping of magnetic field lines and surge seen best in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 171 near N30E60; the signature in SDO AIA 171 is particularly clear, as there is widely opening field line movement off the northeast limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using primarily SOHO C2/C3 and a few STEREO A frames; the measurement fit the observed source on the disk well.

note: CME with an auriform presentation in both the outline of its bulk and shock, seen to the west in SOHO. Associated with a strong eruption from AR 13844 near S10W50 following an M6.7-class flare; an EUV wave is seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO leading edge measurement using a fixed, known longitude based on the source eruption in EUV imagery; the CME is not visibly seen in STEREO A imagery easily, especially during an ongoing STEREO A campaign, but it may potentially be seen to the southeast in STEREO A imagery.
Measurement of shock front using only SOHO imagery, since the CME is not visible well in STEREO A.

note: Narrow, faint CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-03T22:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this CME is a minor filament eruption beginning at approximately 03/20:30Z centered at N35E50 as seen in SDO AIA 171 and 304, although the CME itself appears to be deflected towards the North. Minor field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171 and 193 as a result of this eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-03T23:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this eruption, however faint field line movement can be seen along the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 195 beginning at approximately 03/22:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: This CME is faintly visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and to the south in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be two eruptions in close proximity to each other in the SW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk. A dimming region possibly associated with a faint filament eruption is visible in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2024-10-04T02:00Z in the SW near ARs 13842, 13839, and 13844 followed by moving/opening field lines visible in SDO/AIA 171 starting around 2024-10-04T03:00Z in the SW below ARs 13844, 13843, and 13836. The moving/opening field lines are largely visible heading to the west while the dimming appears to have some southern directionality. A third separate eruption from AR 13842 (an M4.0 flare) is likely associated with an overlapping CME feature. There is some uncertainty with this analysis due to the multiple eruptions in close proximity and timing to when the CME is first visible in coronagraph imagery. Both SOHO and STEREO A coronagraphs have data gaps during this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of faint leading edge in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery. There is a high level of uncertainty with this analysis due to multiple nearly simultaneous eruptions leading up to the CME in imagery. The width of the CME is very uncertain.

note: A southern CME with a somewhat uncertain front seen with some uncertainty overlapping with the earlier 2024-10-04T04:13Z CME and discernible mostly in difference imagery (not clearly seen in white light images). It is likely associated with the M4.0 flare from Active Region 3842 and the associated narrow, south-directed ejecta seen in AIA/SUVI 304 starting at 2024-10-04T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. Parameters are uncertain because the CME front is not clear as it is overlapping with the preceding wider CME.

note: CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-04T06:24Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The likely source of this CME is a very minor eruption from AR 3838 (N1W52) beginning at approx. 04/05:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 193, although the CME is likely slightly deflected Northward. Minor field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Few STEREO A frames were usable for this measurement due to the faintness of the CME.

note: Faint loop CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-04T10:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The likely source of this CME is field line movement seen in the vicinity of S35W30 beginning at approximately 04/09:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-04T13:25Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is an eruption from the vicinity of AR 3844 (S15W37) beginning at approximately 04/12:30Z, although the CME itself appears to exhibit Southern deflection. Field line opening can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 171 along with post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: A wide CME directly north in STEREO A coronagraph and a bit towards NNE in SOHO. There is a wider shock and a narrower brighter bulk. The shock looks like an asymmetric halo with additional part seen to the west in COR2A. There was no source found on the Earth-facing disk so the CME is likely backsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. It incorporates the most faint western part of the halo in STEREO A COR2.

Very approximate analysis based only on the fit with two coronagraphs (since no source has been found in the EUV imagery). Latitude could be lower or higher (at least from 30 deg to 50 deg) but ~40 degrees seems to produce the best fit.

note: A very diffuse front with many follow up emission. The source may be a broad field line movement over the NW limb beginning as early as 2024-10-04T23Z but the source is unclear.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate POS measurement. The front is so fuzzy that it is difficult to fit it with both coronagraphs.

note: A very faint front only seen in running difference imagery from SOHO (C2 and C3), but not discernible in the white light SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 imagery (which is sparse and low quality because of the currently STEREO campaign). No definitive source has been found for this CME. This front is followed by multiple similar faint fronts.
A very faint and narrow outflow to the south and southwest.  The source has not been found - but there is a lot of activity in the SW quadrant which may be obscuring the source.

cmeAnalyses.note: An uncertain measurement based on fit with two coronagraph and not confirmed by the source location (source not found).

note: CME seen to the SW in all coronagraphs. The source for this CME is uncertain, with no one distinct eruptive source and the entire southwest quadrant of SDO AIA 171 imagery observing broad field line movement from as early as 4Z this morning, likely due to the numerous active regions in the SW and SW limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to the uncertain source, and poor image quality in STEREO COR2A running difference imagery with an ongoing campaign that cannot resolve the diffuse CME front.

note: CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and in STEREO COR2A white light imagery. The source is a thin jet-like filament eruption from on or just beyond the SW limb, best observed erupting at 2024-10-05T11:52Z in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using only SOHO LASCO C3, as the CME deflects in C2 and cannot be traced, and STEREO COR2A campaign data is very poor running difference quality and unfortunately not usable to triangulate this source which may lie just barely beyond the limb. However, this POS analysis is likely close to the true source, which is directed well out of the ecliptic.

note: A very faint front - one of multiple faint fronts today - that is mainly seen in difference imagery and has no clear source in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Uncertain analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and not confirmed by source location (no source has been found).

note: Bright CME to the northwest. Its source is likely the inconspicuous  opening of field lines in the northwest behind the limb seen in AIA 193/171 after 2024-10-05T19:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs, not confirmed by the source location since the source is behind the limb. The longitude could be at least -10 to +10 degrees off.
Stereo data are very sparse and low quality because of the ongoing campaign so the SOHO based POS analysis is in order.

note: Faint, narrow CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T04:48Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME appears to get overtaken by CME: 2024-10-06T06:12Z. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this event, however some very minor field line opening can be seen in GOES SUVI 284 at approx. 06/04:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. CME had been over taken by the time it entered SOHO LASCO C3. CME exhibits strong Southern deflection.

note: Faint, fast CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T05:48Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is seen overlapping with CME: 2024-10-06T04:48Z and CME: 2024-10-06T06:12Z. There is no clear source seen on the disk as this CME is likely far sided, however minor field line movement can be seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T06:12Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. There is no abundantly clear source seen on the disk, however some faint field line opening can be seen near the SW limb in SDO AIA 193 and 211 beginning at approx. -6/05:30Z. This CME is seen overtaking CME: 2024-10-06T04:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint, somewhat asymmetric, CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T16:12Z. No clear source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: An extremely approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, however the sole STEREO A image showing the front of this CME after the data gap is very poor quality, in addition to the source of this CME no having been found in EUV imagery.

note: A faint narrow outflow towards northwest. No clear source have been found for it, although there is a lot of activity in the western part of the disk today. The CME is not seen in STEREO imagery because of a large data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Since there is no STEREO A imagery available for this event because of a large data gap only POS analysis is definitive.

note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-07T03:48Z. Also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is like some activity from the vicinity of AR 3841. There is some minor brightening and movement along field lines best seen in SDO AIA 171 starting about 1.5 hours prior to the CME appearing in C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-07T04:36Z. The source of this CME is possibility related to some faint field line movement from beyond the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2024-10-07T03:50Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2 using SWPC_CAT.

note: Wide, bright CME seen to the southwest in SOHO C2/C3 seemingly composed of two or more overlapping loops with internal structure clearly visible and no cavity. Presence of very faint shock may possibly be seen due south in LASCO C2 running difference imagery and may begin to reveal itself to the north-northeast in late SOHO frames after 22:30Z, though disjoint from the main CME body. Associated with a sympathetic eruption resulting from the long duration X2.1/X1.0-class flares (AR3842) located farther behind the southwestern limb than where the X2.1 takes place (W60) as seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery; the CME appears to originate closer to the southwestern limb. Fast, widely opening field lines are also observed in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREOCat one-spacecraft (SOHO) bulk measurement with plane of sky angle set to -2 degrees in order to fix longitude; SWPC_Cat measurements of the leading edge of the CME best fit longitudes near 45 degrees west given the CMEs rounded appearance and presence in the south, which were felt to be unrealistic given the source location of the eruption.

Shock measurement using one spacecraft (SOHO) C2 and C3 images which fits the widest extent of the south and southwestern portions of the CME leading edge as well as a north-northeastern portion that reveals itself in later SOHO frames after 22:30Z which is assumed to be part of the CME shock, though it is disjoint. This measurement is in support of solar energetic particle modeling activities, and as such, is not an approximation of the source location and should not be used for trajectory analysis.

note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery for a few frames prior to a data gap starting at 2024-10-08T03:38Z. The source may be related to field line movement visible near the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery around 2024-10-08T00:40Z. Additionally, there are rising loops/possible post-eruptive arcades visible near the western limb around 01:00Z in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193 imagery which may also be related to this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and is visible in STEREO A COR2 for a few frames prior to a data gap beginning at 2024-10-08T03:38Z. The source is likely related to an eruption near S19W72 starting around 2024-10-08T01:54Z seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is limited imagery for this event and various CME fronts/outflow features that make it difficult to track the leading edge in coronagraph imagery. Because of this the measured parameters may vary slightly.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, and is only visible in STEREO A COR2 after the leading edge is out of the field of view due to a data gap from 2024-10-08T03:38Z to 09:23Z. The source is a large filament eruption centered near S25W30 which begins to erupt, deflecting southward, around 2024-10-08T05:20Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery at the time of the eruption, and post-eruptive arcades begin to form around 06:30Z in SDO AIA131, 171, and 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the approximate source location. There is uncertainty in this measurement due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery and limited imagery in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The measured parameters may therefore vary slightly.

note: CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and a few frames of STEREO A COR2 prior to a data gap starting at 2024-10-08T13:23Z. The source is likely far-sided, and seen as faint opening of field lines visible beyond the eastern limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2024-10-08T11:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and an early frame of STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT, as well as candidate source location beyond the limb. This measurement is approximate, and the longitude may vary by approximately +/- 10 degrees.

note: Relatively narrow CME first seen in the East initially by STEREO A COR2, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in later frames. This event gets quickly overtaken by the X1.8-flare-associated halo 2024-10-09T02:12Z CME. The source of this event is possibly a more minor flare sympathetic to the X flare happening at the same time in Active Region 3853 (N20E63) with post-eruptive arcades or more minor opening field lines and slight dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 originating from the vicinity of AR 3852 (S14E53). This more minor flare is not measurable since it coincides with the more intense flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate measurement based on the fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by the possible location of the source (dimming). Only a few timestamps are available for this front in coronagraphs.

note: Bright, fast and complex-shaped full halo CME associated with the X1.8 class flare from the Active Region 13848 (N13W08). The CME has two lobes or fronts: the more western, slightly earlier one, and the more central on to the northeast. The flare is associated with the significant eruption marked by an EUV wave, a large area of deep dimming and by bright post-eruptive arcades. There also  seems to be a second eruption - the initially slowly developing eruption of a very large filament spanning from N20W15 to N15W55, to the northwest of the Active Region 3848, which starts prior to the X flare (~2024-10-08T22:19Z). This earlier eruption may be responsible for the more western lobe or front of this CME (which could possibly be a separate CME). The X-class flare could be potentially be responsible for the more central, northeastern lobe/front of this complex event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two-coronagraph analysis of the complex-shaped (two-lobed) brighter front we consider to be the bulk of this CME. This analysis is based on the location of the X flare as the source, which is confirmed by a good fit with two coronagraphs. This analysis encompasses both the more eastern lobe/front of this CME and the more western lobe, which are best seen in LASCO C2.
SHOCK measurement made using running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Two-coronagraph analysis of the more central front/lobe of the complex halo CME seen in coronagraphs. This analysis is based on fitting in two coronagraphs of the more eastern lobe of this complex CME event, the source of which is the X-class flare.  Note that the more western lobe is considered in this analysis to be a separate, 2024-10-09T02:23Z, CME associated with a large filament erupting to the west of the Active Region 13848 prior to the X flare.

note: A clear, more western loop especially well seen in SOHO C2 (starting at 2024-10-09T02:12Z) and overlapping with a more central front associated with the Xclass flare. The start time was set to 02:23Z to distinguish it from the more central CME. The source of this more western front is likely the initially slowly developing eruption of a very large filament spanning from N20W15 to N15W55 to the northwest of Active Region 3848 which started prior to the X flare (~2024-10-08T22:19Z). This earlier eruption may be responsible for the more western lobe/front, while the flare could be responsible for the more central, northeastern front of this complex CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two-coronagraph analysis of the western loop-like front/lobe of the complex halo CME complex. Analysis is based on the source location (approximate center of the erupting filament) and confirmed by a decent fit in two coronagraphs. Encompasses only the western lobe/front of this complex (with the more western lobe deemed to be the X-flare associated separate CME).

note: CME visible to the W/NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and a few frames of STEREO A COR2 after a data gap in STEREO A COR2 lasting from 2024-10-09T13:53Z to 2024-10-09T18:53Z. This CME is associated with the X1.4 flare from AR 13842 (S10W85) close to the SW limb. There is a narrow stream of ejecta visible in GOES SUVI 304 sourced from AR 13842 but deflected to the north and off the limb. Source is likely a small jet-like eruption of material seen on or just beyond the NW limb (W90-W110) and at about N15 in GOES SUVI 304 (seen most clearly at later frame 2024-12-03T20:56Z) immediately following an on-limb filament eruption which had likely resulted in a preceding northwest CME: 2024-12-03T20:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate location of source as observed in UV imagery and based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 frames. This CME was not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to overnight data gap which lasted from 2024-12-03T12:23Z to 2024-12-04T00:38Z.

note: Faint CME to the SE seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Source is an M2.3 flare with peak time 2024-12-04T10:00Z as well as rising and opening loops of field lines which begin simultaneously with the flare and from the same location, as seen in GOES SUVI 131. The location of this source is an unnumbered region directly on the East limb, located at S10E90 at the time of the flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of faint leading edge using C2 and COR2A. This CME was not visible in C3 difference imagery; it was nearly entirely blocked by the pylon and the partial edge that could be seen was extremely faint and unreliable to track. The leading edge is faint and quickly becomes diffuse in both C2 and COR2A.

note: This CME is visible to the east/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely an eruption visible near the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery starting around 2024-12-05T00:30Z. A rising loop is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 171 and dimming is visible near the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 195 imagery around this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint CME with diffuse leading edge seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO and north in STEREO A; likely associated with far-side activity, though could possibly be associated with a point source eruption located near N35E02, with some flickering field lines in the north seen around 02:45Z in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft measurement using triangulation to determine longitude.

note: CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO/STEREO A COR2 associated with an M2.5-class solar flare and subsequent eruption from near Active Region 3906 occupying very close to the southwestern limb. The CME becomes appear bright in initial imagery and well-defined and becomes more diffuse with time, eventually losing its leading edge.

cmeAnalyses.note: Bulk measurement as the leading edge becomes diffuse with time, utilizing both SOHO and STEREO A for triangulation.

note: Fast CME with protruding/faster nose seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO during a STEREO A COR2 data gap. Likely associated with far-sided activity as evidenced by moving field lines seen off the southeast limb in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary leading edge measurement using one spacecraft (SOHO) which considers a large latitude to fit visual observations; uncertainty in longitude is quite large and may be as large as +/- 30 degrees.

note: CME seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only, missed in STEREO COR2A due to a data gap spanning this event. The source for this CME appears to be far-sided, and may be continued outflow following the larger, fast CME 2024-12-05T15:48Z which was analyzed far-sided to S47E124. Field line movement over the SSE limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2024-12-05T16:30Z may correlate to this event, but this movement may just be continued from 2024-12-05T15:48Z as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Plane-of-sky measurement with only SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap in STEREO COR2A and the uncertain longitude of this likely far-sided source, via observations in GOES SUVI 171 and 284.

note: Very faint CME first seen in the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-12-05T20:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap from 2024-12-05T12:09Z to 2024-12-06T00:38Z. The source of this event is clear field line opening seen along or just beyond the SW limb as seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS measurement due to source near the limb and lack of available STEREO A imagery to triangulate

note: Faint CME with a fairly narrow shape but a type of "hook" at the end visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery (more easily identified in difference imagery). cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit between SOHO and STEREO A difference imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be a filament eruption near N10E60 as seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 06/01:15Z with associated moving/opening field lines visible in GOES SUVI 284 and dimming in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of CME in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint, outflow-like CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. This CME was not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which lasted from 2024-12-06T15:53Z to 2024-12-06T19:53Z. Source is subtle and slow field line movement from on or beyond the SW limb, seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2024-12-06T13:00Z with a slightly more distinct outflow of material seen at about 14:10Z. Opening field lines on the SW limb can also be seen in GOES SUVI 195 at 14:20Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement of the leading edge made using SWPC CAT. Several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 were used. Leading edge becomes too diffuse to track only after a handful of C3 frames. This CME was not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which lasted from 2024-12-06T15:53Z to 2024-12-06T19:53Z.

note: Very faint, puff-like CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge becomes completely diffuse before reaching halfway through C2's field-of-view. The source is uncertain. One candidate source is an area of dimming seen centered at about N10W40 starting at 2024-12-06T18:00Z in GOES SUVI 284, accompanied by a small amount of brightening from AR 13910 (N16W60) and/or AR 13918 (N13W57). Another candidate source is subtle field line movement on or beyond the NW limb seen in GOES SUVI 284/195. This CME was not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which lasted from 2024-12-06T15:53Z to 2024-12-06T19:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2 imagery, due to lack of COR2A and uncertainty of source location. The leading edge becomes completely diffuse before reaching halfway through C2's FOV.

note: This CME is faintly visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: These parameters are based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO and STEREO A coronagraph imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the W/NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There are a lot of overlapping fronts following the initial front of this CME. There are two potential sources, one is moving/opening field lines beyond the limb as seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 02:30Z. There is also some movement in the AR's 13912 and 13913 starting around 02Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the best fit with two coronagraphs.

note: Faint jet-like/outflow-like CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be a very small faint eruption near N20E60 as seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2024-12-07T03:50Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery.

note: Faint front overlapping with the 2024-12-07T04:12Z CME. No clear source was found for this CME on the Earth-facing disk, although there is minor activity from the Active Region 13913 and north of it going on all morning.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The front in STEREO A COR2 is super faint and fuzzy.

note: Faint jet-like/outflow-like CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be a very small faint eruption near N20E60 as seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2024-12-07T06:50Z. (Follows very similar path to the CME first seen at 2024-12-07T04:24Z).

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: A faint narrow CME in the southwest following the 2024-12-07T04:12Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs.

note: Initially bright but very messy front to the SW in COR2A and C2. The source is the wide opening/movement of field lines on/behind the SW limb in EUVI A 195 (so at longitudes >=120 deg) around 20:05Z. The (very messy) ejecta/filament eruption is also seen in EUVI A 304 on/behind the limb at 2024-12-07T20:15Z after a data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a small eruption from Active Region 13916 (S16E13) starting around 2024-12-08T04:10Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery which appears to deflect towards the southeast.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Flux rope CME with an additional narrow portion on the southern edge that protrudes in front of the leading edge of the main flux rope shape seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Ejecta can also be seen in GOS SUVI 304 which can first be seen starting at 2024-12-08T09:24Z, but was likely initiated with the flare. Flare, dimming, and ejecta can also be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 at 2024-12-08T09:05Z and 09:15Z, respectively.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2; fits very well to source location (~S10W50) observed in UV imagery.

note: CME faintly seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is unclear, and may be one of several minor candidate source eruptions on the disk, including some brightening from AR 3917 (near S05E05) starting around 2024-12-09T01:56Z in GOES SUVI 195 or some faint dimming starting around 2024-12-09T01:00Z around S50E10 in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT. The CME is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk which agree with the measured longitude of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a faint and minor eruption centered near S50E40 as seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery around 2024-12-09T23:10Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge becomes too diffuse to measure after a few frames, and the measured parameters rely on early imagery as a result.

note: Narrow CME associated with a thin, southward deflecting ejecta seen in the SSE in SUVI 304 around 02:52 and possibly associated with the C9.7 from AR 3922. This southward directed deflection of ejecta and CME is peculiar to today's events from Active Region 3922.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with 2 coronagraphs, somewhat contradicting the location of the flare (long ~-77 deg). Analysis is complicated by a large data gap in SOHO, as well as by the partial obscuring of this CME by SOHO C3 pylon. Longitude of the CME could be as high as -70 degrees (with a different fit with 2 coronagraphs in the tool)

note: A relatively narrow CME associated withthe M6.4 flare from AR 3922 (S18E72), with a narrow southward-deflecting ejecta from this AR seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2024-12-10T04:48Z. Because the sequence of flare/ejecta/CME events is very fast for this and the 2024-12-10T07:24Z CME the attribution to the linked flare is not absolutely certain.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by the location of the associated flare.

note: This CME is likely associated with the M1.4 flare from AR 3922 (S18E72) and is also associated with a thin southward-deflecting ejecta from this AR seen in the southwest in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting at 2024-12-10T07:16Z but best seen after 07:28Z. Because the sequence of flare/ejecta/CME events is very fast for this and the 2024-12-10T07:00Z CME (which is associated to the preceding M5.6 flare from the same active region), the exact attribution to the linked flare for these two CMEs is not absolutely certain.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by location of the flare.

note: A very slow CME/outflow that follows even slower outflows/fronts that start as early as 2024-12-10T02Z. The source of it could be continuous activity in AR 3920 since this morning (~ location N22E37 at 02Z) which is marked by brightening in SUVI 195. After 08Z there is a minor dimming around this Active Region which could mark the eruption that might be associated with the 2024-12-10T09:53Z front.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit in two coronagraphs and later confirmed by the possible source (continuous activity all morning culminating with 08Z dimming in AR 3920).

note: Narrow CME associated with M1.5 flare from AR 3922 (S18E72) and a narrow but eventually fan-shaped wide, south-deflecting ejecta from this AR seen in the southeast in SUVI 304/284 and on southeast limb in EUVI A 195 starting at 2024-12-10T11:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. It differs a bit from the location of the associated flare, so there is some westward deflection, in addition to significant southward deflection.

note: This CME is visible to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery and at least one frame of STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a data gap for the majority of this event in STEREO A COR2 imagery with the exception of a single frame at 2024-12-10T14:38Z. The source is unclear but could be a small eruption from AR 13920.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and one frame in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is high uncertainty due to lack of clear source and having only one frame in STEREO A COR2 imagery of this CME.

note: This CME is visible to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and possibly C3. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery for the duration of this event. The source appears to be a C2.8 flare from AR 13920 (N22E27) with a visible eruption and associated filament ejecta starting around 2024-12-10T14:10Z in GOES SUVI 304 and 131 with the ejecta deflected NE.

cmeAnalyses.note: This analysis is based off of the best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. The front becomes too diffuse/faint to track before it exits the C2 field of view. It is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C3 difference imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery for this event. The source appears to be far-sided with moving/opening field lines visible along the S/SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2024-12-10T15:42Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-Sky analysis based on best fit of CME in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery using SWPC_CAT. The front deflects further south as it progresses out in the C2 field of view.

note: This CME is visible to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery for the duration of this event. The potential source for this CME is an eruption with filament ejecta from AR 13920 (N22E24) starting around 2024-12-10T16:20Z in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: These parameters are based on the potential source location (accounting for deflection of source to the NE) and the best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery. The front has a diffuse front making for tricky analysis.

note: This CME is visible to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and possibly C3. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery for the duration of this event. The source appears to be a filament ejecta eruption from AR 13920 (N22E28) starting around 2024-12-10T17:08Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304 with deflection to the NE.

cmeAnalyses.note: These parameters are based on the potential source location (accounting for deflection of source to the NE) and the best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery. The front is pretty diffuse in SOHO LASCO C2 difference imagery but becomes slightly more clear in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery, however there are overlapping features making this analysis a bit uncertain.

note: This CME is visible to the S/SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery for this event. The source appears to be an M1.6 class flare from AR 13922 (S18E70) with a sympathetic eruption to the west of this region starting around 2024-12-10T17:58Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 304, and 284. Moving/opening field lines are visible along the limb as well as a minor EUV wave to the south along the limb as seen in GOES SUVI 284 and 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: This CME deflects far to the south with continued deflection southward as it progresses through the SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 field of view. Due to this, there is some uncertainty with the fit.

note: This CME is visible to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery for the duration of this event. The source for this CME is possibly a small eruption from AR 13920 (N22E21) starting around 2024-12-10T20:58Z as seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based off of the best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 using the potential source location for longitude and adjusting the latitude to fit the CME.

note: Narrow CME to the northeast, with messy, fuzzy, dimpled front. This CME islikely associated with minor activity in AR 13920 (N15E23).

cmeAnalyses.note: Based on the fit with two coronagraphs, which confirms the source location as the location of the likely associated Active Region 3920 which is showing some minor activity.

note: Relatively slow and wide CME seen to the south in SOHO LASCO imagery and southeast in STEREO A COR2. Very similar in appearance to the far-sided 2024-12-11T12:12Z CME, there are a few sources on the Earth-facing disk including an eruption on the western portion of the disk, but triangulation strongly suggests this event is far-sided. No candidate sources for this CME were observed in EUV imagery. The CME is quite difficult to measure in LASCO C2 with the CME off the southeast (CME: 2024-12-11T06:24Z) obscuring the CME in question (more evidence this is far-sided).

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft leading edge measurement using triangulation with difficulty seeing the CME leading edge in SOHO LASCO C2 due to an obscuring CME in front of the CME in question; GONG data supports the eruption coming from a far-sided source with this approximate longitude.

note: Another CME with an asymmetric shape in the "AR 3922 style". It is associated with the M1.9 flare from AR 3922 (S17E55), however the opening of field lines we see in in SUVI 284 seems to be further south from AR 3922. There is also opening of field lines in SUVI 171 closer to this AR.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit in two coronagraphs but confirmed by source location (taking into account southward deflection).

note: Minor CME with messy/fuzzy front with the possible source a lower C-class flare from Active Region 3920, with very minor dimming/possibly faint ejecta seen in GOES SUVI 193/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs.

note: Narrow CME with fuzzy front to the northeast, with no clear front in SOHO LASCO C2 and likely associated with the M2.7 flare from Active Region 3920 (N22E18) and the narrow NNE ejecta seen at 2024-12-11T10:36 in SUVI 304 at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, confirmed by the location of the associated flare.

note: Possible partial halo CME seen as two separate portions, a portion to the south and southeast visible in SOHO LASCO C2 as well as a portion to the northeast connected by a very faint front to the east. cmeAnalyses.note: One-spacecraft measurement attempting to fit both the south/south-southeast bulk measurement as well as the northeast portion in the SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph.

note: Far-sided halo CME with brighter bulk seen to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and also a fainter, torus-shaped shock with wider extent in the equatorial regions. Likely associated with far-sided activity as evidenced by expulsion and rapidly flickering field lines as seen off the south limb best in GOES SUVI 284 around 2024-12-11T21:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Shock front measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 incorporating the southeastward leading edge and western/eastern leading edges simultaneously in one circular-shaped measurement.
Bulk measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 mainly focusing on brighter south portion of the CME.

note: CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO and north in STEREO A COR2 with faster/protruding leading edge/nose feature. Likely associated with far-sided activity as few, if any, sources were observed in GOES SUVI on the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft bulk measurement capturing the main shape of the CME inside of the protruding feature (i.e. the CME could be faster than this measurement).

note: Relatively slow and minor CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery, seemingly associated with point-source eruption from AR 3916 (S14W46) with some southward deflection as seen in GOES SUVI 304. Not seen well in STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft measurement of the leading edge, holding the known longitude constant.

note: This CME is visible to the west/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery following a data gap from 2024-12-12T15:36Z to 23:24Z. Following the data gap, the CME is visible well into the SOHO LASCO C2/C3 field of view, so the start time is likely earlier than the time stated. This event is visible in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap ending at 2024-12-13T00:53Z for only a few frames. The source is a slow-rising loop visible near or slightly beyond the southwest limb which erupts around 2024-12-12T23:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb at this time in GOES SUVI 171 and 195 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and limited STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery following a data gap from 2024-12-12T15:36Z to 23:24Z. Following the data gap, the CME is visible into the SOHO LASCO C2/C3 field of view, so the start time is likely a bit earlier than the time stated. This event is visible in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap ending at 2024-12-13T00:53Z for only a few frames. The source is an eruption visible from beyond the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2024-12-12T23:16Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and the south/southwest in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a C2.1 flare starting at 2024-12-13T02:21Z from old Active Region 3916 (currently a plage), around S15W55. The eruption is best seen with brightening and an ejecta of material in GOES SUVI 304. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUV 195/304. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Reanalysis of this event in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A going more northern and less wide, noting difficulty in tracking the same faint front between both coronagraphs on top of limited STEREO COR2A availaibility.
Only two frames of STEREO A COR2 were available for this measurement, so this measurement is primarily based off of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery.

note: CME visible to the south/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Partially overlaps in the field of view of the coronagraphs with CME: 2024-12-13T02:48Z. The source is likely an M1.0 flare starting at 2024-12-13T03:11Z from AR 3922 (S18E37) with dimming, opening field lines best seen in GOES SUVI 195/284 as well as an ejecta of material in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 as well as source location in SWPC_CAT. Only one frame of STEREO A COR2 was available for a measurement, and the majority of the measurement uses SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: CME visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around S35E30 with liftoff starting around 2024-12-13T06:48Z as best seen in GOES SUVI 304. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.

note: Narrow CME faintly visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2024-12-13T11:38Z. The source is not clearly visible in available EUV imagery, and the CME may originate from the far side.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Wide CME seen predominantly to the south in SOHO LASCO imagery during a STEREO A data gap. May be potentially associated with an M1.0 flare from AR 3922 starting at 2024-12-13T14:15Z, but there is no clear eruption of material leading to a CME associated with it. There is some faint dimming seen in GOES SUVI 284 at 14:26Z, close in time to when this was in the coronagraphs. Initial analysis suggests this eruption originates from the far-side, but triangulation with STEREO A data is probably necessary to confirm front-sidedness.

In EUVI A 195 near the west limb (in STEREO) there are post-eruptive arcades seen at ~2024-12-15T01:05Z after the long data gap. cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery and potential source location.

The source of this event appears to be an area of dimming centered near AR 3924 (S19W18) as seen GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2. Measurements with similar parameters using possible front seen in SOHO LASCO C3 were also made, but with lower confidence.

note: Faint CME overlapping a bright streamer to the W/SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C-class flare and associated filament ejecta from decayed AR 13916 (S15W85) visible in GOES SUVI 304, 284, 131, and STEREO A EUVI 304 starting around 2024-12-15T09:30Z.

A portion of the front appears to be moving faster than the rest of the CME which may be indicative of an overlapping CME. cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 using SWPC_CAT. This CME is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2024-12-18T11:38Z to 2024-12-18T16:38Z.

S05W70 to S22W65, near Active Region 3924 (S20W65). Part of this CME is not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2024-12-18T11:38Z to 2024-12-18T16:36Z.

There is some minor influence seen in the NE quadrant of the Earth-facing disk, but this eruption appears much more likely to be far-sided. A far-sided source is also consistent with measurements.

The source of this CME is likely a small amount of activity and brightening starting about 2024-12-19T01:45Z best seen in GOES SUVI 304 on the W limb at about N10. The source of this CME is a filament eruption from on or beyond the SW limb. The prominence material can be seen lifting off the SW limb in both GOES SUVI 284 and 304 starting about 2024-12-19T12:53Z. This filament eruption is overtaken by a far-sided halo CME with start time 2024-12-19T17:53Z in STEREO A COR2. This CME is only discernible by itself in SOHO LASCO C2 and a couple of frames in SOHO LASCO C3. The majority of the CME is obscured by and blends in with the far-sided halo later in its propagation into the fields-of-view of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

This start time was chosen based on when the CME was first seen in available imagery at the time of analysis, but the actual start time is earlier. The source of this CME is most likely far-sided. There are no good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk, and coronal signatures from beyond the SW limb suggest a far-sided source.  In GOES SUVI 284, there is some flickering in the farthest out field lines over the SW limb across most of the SW quadrant first seen at about 2024-12-19T16:19Z. There is also some very faint ejecta seen from beyond the SW limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting about 2024-12-19T16:21Z. Measurements are consistent with a far-sided source. This CME also overlaps with a prior filament eruption to the SW.

Based on the measurement, the filament near S40W35 seems to be better the source candidate.

The source is likely related to an eruption and subsequent M2.0 flare from Active Region 13939 (S17E30) starting around 2024-12-29T04:20Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. A subsequent dimming is observed around the eruption site in GOES SUVI 195 imagery at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the brighter, bulk portion of this event based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement of the faint, outermost SHOCK feature based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk which fit this event between coronagraphs.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely related to an eruption visible just on the southeast limb starting around 2024-12-29T11:00Z seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the southeast limb at this time as well, as seen in GOES SUVI 171, 193, and 284 imagery,

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location.

note: Jet CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 during a STEREO A data gap; associated with an unknown source, potentially far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO plane of sky measurement of the leading edge.

note: Minor CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, associated with a minor filament erupting near N40W55 seen best in GOES SUVI 304/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Bulk measurement of the CME using SOHO C2; the leading edge becomes very diffuse with time.

note: Partial halo seen as a faint leading edge without much overflowing material behind the leading edge, seen to the south and southeast in SOHO LASCO and east-southeast in STEREO A COR2. Likely associated with an eruption from AR3939 near S18E15 seen as quickly breaking field lines near the active region seen best in GOES SUVI 131, 195, 284, 304. The attached WSA-Enlil+Cone simulation should not be interpreted as a forecast and is likely to overestimate geomagnetic impacts at Earth given that the measurement represents the faint shock associated with the CME, which does not contain much observed material behind the leading edge.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the faint shock front using triangulation between STEREO A and SOHO; simulation is likely to overestimate geomagnetic impacts at Earth given there is not much observed material behind the leading edge.

note: A faint very slowly developing partial halo CME to the southwest, with filamentary structures seen in coronagraph and with multiple consecutive fronts. There is activity on/close to the SW limb early in the morning (opening/movement of field lines close to the limb and some dimming/brightening), but it is happening after 01:30Z and so is unlikely to be the source of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on fit with two coronagraphs (since no clear source was found on disk).

note: CME seen in the northwest in both coronagraph. It has a wider, likely shock, front in addition to a narrower bulk. Its likely source is the X1.5 flare from AR 3936 (N13W46) which was associated with the eruption seen in GOES SUVI 195/284 as rising post eruptive arcades and some dimming. There are also moving of field lines closer to the northwest limb seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis is based on the fit with two coronagraphs but also incorporates the location of the likely source of this CME, the flare.

note: Very faint CME first seen in the SE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2024-12-30T10:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2 in later frames. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2 and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this event is an eruption seen near AR 3939 (S17E15) with post-eruptive arcades and dimming  seen in SUVI 195/284 after 08:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This event is not being simulated as it fades after a few frames in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: CME first seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-12-31T00:12Z. Also visible to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C3. This CME might be very faintly visible STEREO A COR2 for two frames, but it is not definitively this CME. A possible source candidate is some minor brightening and activity from AR 3936 starting about 21:48Z visible in all GOES SUVI wavelengths, but measurement does not closely match this source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 using SWPC_CAT.

note: Thin, fast CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source is field line movement and a small post eruptive arcade observed just inside the the NW limb (~N15W89) starting around 2024-12-31T12:56Z in GOES SUVI 171/195/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. This front appears to be slightly less than a halfwidth of 10, and also triangulated slightly further on-disk than the source observed in GOES SUVI imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a dimming region centered near S25E40 starting around 2024-12-31T13:15Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171 and imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and is not observed STEREO COR2A due to a data gap starting at 2024-12-31T15:38Z. The source may be related to field line movement on the northwest limb (~N15) starting around 2024-12-31T16:24Z in GOES SUVI 171/195/284 followed by a small post eruptive arcade.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees. A triangulated measurement was not available due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event.
